info.name: DX DataBank onboarding + job approval flow
info.description:
NOTE: the infra-provider flow is a dummy for now (collection variable skip_infra_flow = "true"): A2, 1d and 2c are skipped and the infra checks in 3a are off - only the data-provider side is checked. Pairs with REQUIRE_INFRA_APPROVAL=false in p3dx_gov_layer/.env.

End-to-end flow: data provider onboards a DataBank in the DX catalogue, consumer creates a job (draft contract) on it, data + infra providers approve it - each approval also posts their APD policy and their signature of the contract hash (keys generated on their own machine) - and the governance layer verifies and creates the final contract.

Setup: fill the *_username / *_password variables (or paste full tokens from the dev portal into data_provider_token / infra_provider_token / access_token). Change dataset_name on every run of A1b (catalogue names are unique); A1b saves the new item id into dataset_id.

Services: cp_url = DX Control Plane (dev), gov_url = p3dx_gov_layer (8083), apd_url = p3dx-apd (8082).

Not implemented yet (planned): provider GET inbox of pending jobs, reject, GET job status.

item.name: 1. Consumer creates the job (draft contract)

request.description: The user who requests the job. Saves access_token; used for 1b (generate contract), 3a (job status) and 4 (enable TEE).

Creates the contract with the dataset + infras and its job_id (saved as job_id / contract_id), and stores it in the governance layer with its contract_hash. Each data and infra provider is sent a JOB_REQUEST carrying that hash (1c/1d); they sign it with their own private key and submit it when approving (2b/2c). At 3a, once every approval and signature verifies, the final contract is created - no governance signature is added.

item.name: 2b. Data-provider approval (approve + submit the signed contract hash)

request.description:
Approves the caller's datasets (role and catalogue checks with their own token) and submits their signature of contract_hash (from the job request, 1c). The signature is verified at once (it must be over the contract_hash stored with the contract, and verify with the registered public key) and stored on the contract; then, per accepted dataset, the consumer grant is posted to the local p3dx-apd (grants) and the IUDX APD policy to IUDX_APD_POLICY_URL with this token (iudx_policies). The policy is built from the stored contract (consumer, expiry, workload, trustee, callbackUrl); provider_comment / feedback_to_consumer are optional and copied into it. An IUDX failure doesn't fail the approval - it is reported in iudx_policies.

Before sending, sign on the provider's machine: `scripts/contract-sign.sh approve-request {{data_provider_id}} keys/providers/<name>/private.pem {{job_id}}` and paste the signature into data_provider_signature.

pm.test('signed contract hash submitted', () => pm.expect(d.signature && d.signature.submitted).to.eql(true));
if (d.signature) console.log('signature submitted for', d.signature.items_signed, 'item(s) - cross-verified at', d.signature.verified_at);

item.description:
Each approval call (2b data provider, 2c infra provider) approves that provider's own items (role and catalogue checks with their own token) and submits their signature of the contract hash from the job request. The data provider's signature is verified at once against the contract_hash stored with the contract at 1b and their registered public key - a bad one is refused and nothing is recorded. On acceptance 2b also posts, for each of their datasets, the consumer grant to the local p3dx-apd and the IUDX APD policy (IUDX_APD_POLICY_URL, with the data provider's own token). Step 3 cross-verifies every signature again before the job is approved.

item.name: 3. Cross-verify signatures + job status (consumer)

request.description: 1. Every data and infra provider has approved. 2. Each provider's signed contract_hash equals the contract_hash stored with the contract at 1b (itself re-checked against a fresh hash of the stored contract), and their signature verifies with their registered public key. 3. If all hold: the job is approved and its final contract is created in final_contracts (no governance signature), then the APD grant is posted for every dataset and infra (this user may use it for this job_id + contract_id) -> {status: approved, signatures, final_contract: true, final_contract_record}. Otherwise {status: not approved, reasons: [...]}.

item.description: One call, 3a. In order: every provider has approved; the contract_hash stored at 1b still matches the stored contract; every provider signature is over that hash and verifies with their registered public key. Only when all hold is the job approved and its final contract created: stored once in final_contracts (returned as final_contract_record). No governance signature is added - the providers' signatures over the stored hash are what make it final. If any check fails, nothing is created. The APD grants are posted after that.

item.name: 4. Enable the TEE (consumer)
item.description: Once the contract is final, the user who created the job enables the TEE run. This only marks it enabled - no VM is started; the run itself is POST /v1/tee/sessions with governanceContractId = contract_id, which is refused until this step is done.

request.description: Consumer's token (1a). 409 CONTRACT_NOT_SIGNED / CONTRACT_NOT_FINAL until every data and infra provider has approved and signed; 403 for anyone but the job's user.

item.name: 5. Start the TEE (consumer)
item.description: Starts the actual TEE run for the job's final contract, after step 4 has enabled it. Runs in the background on gov_layer: start the p3dx-anon-tee VM -> attest -> run -> poll -> fetch output. Returns 202 with a sessionId at once; follow it with GET {{gov_root}}/v1/tee/sessions/{{tee_session_id}}.

request.description:
gov_root = gov_layer without /api/v1 (the TEE routes are mounted at the server root). governanceContractId = contract_id (from 1b). Saves sessionId as tee_session_id.

Fill before sending: tee_resource_url (https; must equal a dataset's data_url on the signed contract, i.e. the data_url of the dataset's APD policy), tee_image_id and tee_image_hash (the anon workload image and its expected measurement), and optionally tee_consumer_public_key. consumerId, issuedAt and expiresAt are filled by the pre-request script.

403 TEE_NOT_ENABLED until step 4 succeeds; 403 if resourceUrl isn't a dataset on the signed contract; 400 INVALID_CONTRACT if a required field is empty.
